clue.text: Harsh view of retired clergy man in the diocese

indicators.note: the turned clergyman's title sits inside the word for the bishop's seat

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the clergyman's short title is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a clergyman

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dim view of the old vicar who has retired within the diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the clergyman's title round, giving VER; 'view of' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe and harsh are synonyms describing strict, unsparing treatment.

clue.text: Stew caused by stolen marijuana

parts.note: hot is slang for stolen goods
pot is slang for marijuana

explanation.surface: A row brews over cannabis that has been pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: A hotpot is a meat-and-potato stew from Lancashire in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotpot is a slow-cooked casserole, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Smart crane Peter designed, being a skilled craftsman

indicators.note: designed suggests something planned and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peter, a smart builder, designed a crane and shows himself a fine workman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges SMART, CRANE and PETER, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: A master carpenter is a highly skilled woodworker, an expert craftsman.

clue.text: Childish boast of old Scottish chieftain is a lot of gas

parts.note: a child boasting cries 'Me!', wanting the attention
a thane was a clan chief or lord in old Scotland, like Macbeth

explanation.surface: A clan leader's boyish bragging amounts to so much hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is a lot of' joins wordplay to definition; 'a lot of gas' also hints at empty talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a flammable gaseous hydrocarbon, the main part of natural gas.

clue.text: Along the frontier things can't be categorised

definitions.meaning: literally lying along the boundary line between two countries
figuratively, of cases so marginal they fit neither category

explanation.surface: Out on the border, nothing can be neatly classified.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both physically at a boundary and, figuratively, in an uncertain marginal position.

clue.text: The point is that it's a total cessation

definitions.meaning: the punctuation dot ending a sentence

explanation.surface: Someone insists the whole point is that everything has come to a halt.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation mark ending a sentence also names, figuratively, a complete stop to anything.

clue.text: Note with care new source of vitamin A

indicators.note: new tells the solver to make fresh letters from the words, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Read this note carefully: here is a fresh supply of vitamin A.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges NOTE and CARE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotene, the orange pigment in carrots, is converted by the body into vitamin A.

clue.text: Vilify Australian tramp in front of the entrance

indicators.note: in front of places the vagrant's word ahead of the doorway word

parts.note: dero is Australian slang for a derelict or tramp
a gate is an entrance

explanation.surface: Someone abuses a homeless man sleeping by the gate.
explanation.walkthrough: DERO is Australian slang for a down-and-out.
explanation.definitionFit: To derogate is to disparage or detract from someone, much as to vilify them.

clue.text: Got Una to make some confectionery

indicators.note: to make signals the letters are worked into something new, rearranged

explanation.surface: Una was given sweets to prepare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' rearranges GOT and UNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy sweet of sugar, honey and nuts, a type of confection.

clue.text: It suits the Scotchman to a T

parts.note: the letter T as written

explanation.surface: A drink pleases the Scot to perfection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to a T', meaning exactly, splits into TO and T; a tot is a small dram of whisky, which suits a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small measure of spirits, the sort of whisky dram a Scot would welcome.

clue.text: Send Desmond to the allotment

parts.note: Des is the short form of the name Desmond
an allotment is a garden patch rented from the council

explanation.surface: Someone sends Desmond off to work on his vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: A British allotment is a small rented plot for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: To despatch, or dispatch, is to send off.

clue.text: How to include everyone with reverence

indicators.note: to include means the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: A question of how to include everyone respectfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverence' is a verb here, meaning to treat with awe; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallow is to honour as holy, to revere something.

clue.text: Two gamblers are improving rapidly

definitions.meaning: two people who bet, each one a punter, side by side

explanation.surface: A pair of punters are on a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is cryptic: a punter is one who bets, and two of them, joined by 'and', give the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Two bettors joined together read as the phrase meaning continually improving.

clue.text: Meal where gateaux form the centre-piece

indicators.note: the centre-piece of the cake word gives its central letters

explanation.surface: A tea party where cakes are the main attraction on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form the centre-piece' takes the middle three letters of GATEAUX; 'where' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain.

clue.text: Fellows meet a translator of Homer

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
a man is also a fellow

explanation.surface: Some university dons meet a scholar who rendered Homer into English.
explanation.walkthrough: One plural word gives two fellows side by side; 'meet' only joins. George Chapman translated Homer's epics in Elizabethan England.
explanation.definitionFit: George Chapman was the Elizabethan poet whose Homer inspired Keats's sonnet.

clue.text: The lady admits one weaving tool is a family treasure

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the pronoun takes the numeral inside

parts.note: her refers to a lady
I is the Roman numeral for one
a loom is the frame used for weaving

explanation.surface: A woman confesses her old weaving frame is a cherished possession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' puts the Roman one inside the lady's pronoun, making HEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: An heirloom is a valued possession handed down through generations.

clue.text: After the project man becomes mournful

indicators.note: after puts the word for man behind the word for project

parts.note: a plan is a project
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: Following the scheme, a fellow grows sad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'project' looks like the subject, but is the scheme word; 'becomes' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Plangent describes a loud, resonant and melancholy sound, hence sorrowful.

clue.text: He gathers the harvest in the fall

definitions.meaning: from the idiom 'come a ___', meaning to take a heavy fall

explanation.surface: An autumn reaper at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall' suggests autumn harvest time, but refers to the idiom for a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A grower or reaper of crops, and the word in the idiom for falling headlong.

clue.text: Soft greeting from a character in Greece

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A quiet hello from someone in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' joins; 'character' means a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Phi is the twenty-first letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Make some changes when agent comes over speechless

indicators.note: comes over suggests turning over, so the agent word is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
mute means speechless

explanation.surface: Changes happen when the salesman arrives and says nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes over' turns REP into PER; 'when' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To permute is to alter the order or arrangement of things.

clue.text: Anxiety of the Secret Services creates the wrong impression

parts.note: MI5 and MI6, the British intelligence services, are the MIs
apprehension is anxiety

explanation.surface: Nervousness in British intelligence leads to a mistaken belief.
explanation.walkthrough: MI5 and MI6 are the British security and intelligence services; together they are the MIs. 'of' and 'creates' join.
explanation.definitionFit: A misapprehension is a mistaken belief or misunderstanding.

clue.text: A nursing nun

parts.note: the one title belongs both to a senior hospital nurse and to a woman in a religious order

explanation.surface: A nun who works as a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: In British hospitals a senior nurse is called by the same title as a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is used for a senior ward nurse in Britain and for a member of a religious order.

clue.text: Began to write in the Oxford English Dictionary

indicators.note: in places the writing word inside the dictionary's initials

parts.note: OED is the abbreviation for the Oxford English Dictionary
to pen is to write

explanation.surface: Someone started to make an entry in the great dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Began' wants the past tense, which the dictionary's initials around the writing tool supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Opened is a synonym for began, as when a play or meeting gets under way.

clue.text: Work hard to get an advertising catch-phrase

parts.note: to slog is to work hard

explanation.surface: It takes effort to come up with a good jingle for an ad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a memorable motto used in advertising.

clue.text: Doctor put the girls on syrup

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: The doctor prescribed the girls a sweet medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put ... on' sets MO ahead of LASSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left after refining sugar.

clue.text: Fashionable conclusion to a thank-you letter

indicators.note: conclusion to puts the fashionable letter at the end of the thanks

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you
U means upper-class, hence fashionable

explanation.surface: A stylish sign-off to a note of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' is the Greek alphabet one, not a note. TA is British slang for thanks; U means upper-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Where the family can relax

parts.note: a cryptic description of the living room in a house, where everyone sits at ease

explanation.surface: A comfortable spot for the household to unwind.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitting room in a house is where family members rest and unwind.

clue.text: Presented by a compassionate journalist

parts.note: tender means compassionate
ed, an editor, is a journalist

explanation.surface: Something offered by a kindly newspaperman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by a' joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To have tendered is to have formally offered or presented something.
